purpose: Prevent RMD from treating a local-currency long-term yield differential as a pure sovereign credit spread, and freeze the observable source boundary before any fiscal-yield estimation.

observed_yield_source.concept: Long-term interest rate for convergence purposes, Romanian leu, Romania, 10-year maturity, monthly average

germany_10y.concept: German long-term convergence interest rate, euro, 10-year maturity, monthly average
germany_10y.use: candidate common long-rate benchmark/control, not proof of a same-currency Romanian credit spread

euro_area_10y.concept: Euro-area long-term convergence interest rate, euro, 10-year maturity, monthly average
euro_area_10y.use: alternative common euro long-rate benchmark/control; benchmark choice must be frozen before model evaluation

financial_stress.use: external/global-euro financial-stress control candidate; frequency aggregation and vintage must be frozen before estimation

semantic_boundary.prohibited_label: Do not label Romania RON 10y minus Germany/euro-area EUR 10y as a pure sovereign credit spread.
semantic_boundary.reason: The cross-currency yield differential combines sovereign risk with currency, monetary-policy and inflation-expectation components.
semantic_boundary.loop_mapping: The Dynamic Core loop uses sovereign_yield, so a validated yield-response equation could support that node without claiming decomposition of the yield into a pure credit spread.

fiscal_source_boundary.debt: Use the already retained official government_debt_stock reference mode / Eurostat Maastricht-debt source when constructing debt-to-GDP controls.
fiscal_source_boundary.deficit: Require an exact official ESA government net-lending/borrowing or deficit-to-GDP source and retained vintage before opening estimation.
fiscal_source_boundary.frequency_rule: Do not forward-fill low-frequency fiscal ratios into monthly observations and then treat the repeated months as independent fiscal information. A mixed-frequency rule or lower-frequency estimation boundary must be preregistered.
fiscal_source_boundary.no_issuance_proxy: Gross issuance or refinancing need may not be inserted as 'supply pressure' without a separately specified and validated source/stock-flow mapping.

candidate_reformulation.rationale: A yield-level equation is aligned with the feedback-registry sovereign_yield node. A pure spread equation would require a definitionally matched same-currency benchmark or an explicit decomposition not currently observed.

required_before_estimation: Retain exact ECB Romania 10-year convergence-yield series with raw-source hash and vintage.
Retain the ex-ante selected common long-rate benchmark series with raw-source hash and vintage.
Retain the ex-ante selected ECB financial-stress control and a preregistered aggregation rule if daily data are used.
Retain exact fiscal debt and deficit controls with frequency/vintage semantics and GDP denominator source.
Freeze the estimation frequency and mixed-frequency treatment before inspecting predictive results.
Freeze structural-selection window, benchmark baselines and untouched evaluation window before estimation.
prohibited_shortcuts: Call a cross-currency RON-minus-EUR yield differential a pure sovereign credit spread.
Treat debt or deficit coefficients as causal without stronger identification.
Forward-fill annual or quarterly fiscal ratios to monthly frequency and count repeated months as independent fiscal observations.
Choose Germany versus euro-area benchmark after viewing fit.
Choose CISS versus SovCISS after viewing fit.
Insert issuance/refinancing need as yield supply pressure without a separate source and structural contract.
Activate the government issuance-yield feedback loop from in-sample fit.
source_materialisation_gate.pass_effect: Authorises a separately preregistered predictive yield-response selection/validation cycle only; no causal or System Dynamics activation follows automatically.
source_materialisation_gate.fail_effect: Retain the mechanism as CANDIDATE and keep the government issuance-yield loop quantitatively inactive.
